releases.name: opencode: v8.0.2-beta.0
releases.body:
<!-- custom-release-notes:start -->
## What changed (8.x `next` line only)

The 8.0.x-beta packages on the npm `next` dist-tag have been uninstallable
since March (`@opencode-swarm/core@8.0.0-beta.0` published a `workspace:*`
dependency spec). The source-side fix landed earlier (#3163), but no corrected
release could ever ship: the automated release path mis-versioned
(release-please swept the resurrected, tag-less `next` branch's entire history
and proposed 9.0.0-beta.0 — PR #3173, closed unmerged), a force-publish retry
would no-op because committed versions still equal the published broken ones,
and the publish steps masked every publish failure.

This release enables the healing release through the repo's own machinery:

- **release-please config**: root-level `bootstrap-sha` bounds the bootstrap
  sweep past the last BREAKING commit (no more 9.0.0-beta.0 mis-proposal);
  per-component tags plus a `linked-versions` lockstep group (all four
  packages release together at one version — tags render as
  `<component>-v<version>`, e.g. `core-v8.0.2-beta.0`); the dead `branches`
  config array is removed (nothing consumed it).
- **publish workflow**: publish steps now fail loudly (`set -eo pipefail` +
  explicit `exit 1`); the E403/already-exists skip tolerance applies only to
  explicit `force_publish` retries.

## User-visible effect

Once the next release PR merges and publishes, `npm i opencode-swarm@next`
(and the bun equivalent) installs successfully again; the broken betas are
then deprecated (`npm deprecate @opencode-swarm/core@8.0.0-beta.0 …`).

## Notes

- The healing release proposes **8.0.2-beta.0 for all four packages**
  (lockstep), advancing every package past its published version.
- Every future `next`-line release re-releases all four packages together
  (linked-versions semantics — intended).

---

# 8.x release pipeline completion: hardened publish path, fragment tooling, and a clean healing-release changelog

## What

- `release-please-next.yml` publishes can no longer run concurrently (workflow-level `concurrency` group, queue-not-cancel), no longer interpolate the `force_publish` input into shell text (job-level `env: FORCE_PUBLISH`), and refuse to publish from any ref other than `refs/heads/next` before the first `npm publish` executes — the documented `force_publish` dispatch recovery from `next` keeps working.
- The publish-step guardrails are now proven by EXECUTION, not line-shape: a test harness runs each real workflow publish step under a fake `npm` on PATH and asserts the exit codes discriminate npm failure / version-conflict / tolerance / success. The three known neutralization shapes (`set +e` after the required set line, always-true tolerance, `exit 1` nested under a never-true `if`) each ship as executed mutants that neutralize — exactly the class the real-step legs catch.
- Breaking-commit detection in the release-please config guard now scans commit BODIES line-anchored (`^BREAKING[ -]CHANGE:`), closing the false negative where the space-form footer is invisible to git's trailer machinery. The original trailer-leg filter (`key=BREAKING CHANGE`) was executed-proven vacuous (matched neither spelling) and is corrected to the hyphen-key form.
- The bootstrap changelog bound moves from the March breaking commit to the dormant tip `23f051f11`: the healing release PR's changelog now contains only the October 8.x-line changes instead of seven months of dormant-branch noise. `packages/telemetry` (zero post-bound commits) still releases in lockstep via release-please's linked-versions synchronize mechanism — verified from the plugin source and pinned by the rewritten group-coverage test.
- The main line's release-fragment pipeline is ported to the 8.x line: `scripts/release-notes-fragments.mjs` (release-PR body enrichment, per-component-tag GitHub Release body enrichment with a per-package CHANGELOG fallback, and consume-and-remove cleanup whose deletions are anchored to the release merge SHA and the p

## Shell write-gate escape classes + knowledge family migration recency (#3518, #3521)

Closes #3518 and #3521 (collated).

### #3518 — five shell write-gate escape classes (security)

- **Quoted process-substitution operands no longer escape the declared
  scope.** The parse-failure string fallback dequotes exactly-pair-quoted
  operands (matching the AST branch) and withdraws — fail-closed — every
  unresolvable shape: fragmented/unbalanced quoting, quoted destinations
  containing whitespace, backslash-escaped-space operands, multi-redirect
  stages where the lazy capture only sees the last target, and any
  procsub write on a line whose text carries a `cd`/`pushd <target>` word
  (then/do/brace-led forms included).
- **An unprovable `cd` is judged at BOTH landings.** The tracked walk models
  the cd failing (cwd kept); the pessimistic walk models it succeeding at the
  bash-true target (Git Bash `/x/...` drive spellings mapped, landings
  propagated through `&&` chains and control-flow bodies) — the gate requires
  every landing to pass. A `cd` whose target the same command creates
  (`mkdir -p zz && cd zz && …`), grouped/brace/if-body cd forms, and
  Git-Bash drive paths all deny when the success landing is outside the
  declared scope. Known edge: a failing `cd` before `&&` now conservatively
  blocks the never-executed right-side write — fail-closed on an ambiguous
  shape.
- **The process-substitution fallback after a `cd` no longer resolves at the
  starting cwd.** `cd ../.. && true >(truncate -s 0 src/f)` is denied like
  its procsub-free twin (withdrawn, fail-closed). Known edge: this
  over-blocks lines that mix a working `cd` with a parse-failing process
  substitution — bounded to that shape.
- **Same-literal writes separated by a `cd` are each scope-checked at their
  own resolved path.** The #3347 occurrence-suffix is widened to every
  duplicate write (not just capability evals), so `cd src && echo x > f; cd
  ../.. && echo PWN > f` is denied at the second occurrence. Detector
  surfaces now show per-occurrence operators (`> #2`); same-cwd duplicates
  resolve identically at the gate.
- **Parenthesis-led destructive segments reach the live gate arms.** The
  rd/rmdir/del (cmd.exe), rm (POSIX), and Remove-Item (PowerShell) anchors
  tolerate a leading open-paren — glued `(rd x /s)`, spaced `( rd x /s )`,
  and POSIX brace groups `{ rm -rf x; }` — closing the reversed wedge where
  the classifier denied `(rd ../../outside /s)` while the live gate
  admitted it.

### #3521 — knowledge family migration (data-loss class, config-ungated)

- **Same-id merges are recency-aware.** `mergeStoreEntries` and the
  append-union merge keep the NEWER version on a same-id collision
  (`updated_at` with `revision` tiebreak on the store; `updated_at` on
  unactionable; `quarantined_at` on quarantined), destination-newer
  unchanged, no-signal collisions keep the destination and are reported
  (`superseded`/`noSignal` counts added to the migration report). Within-side
  duplicate ids select the effective (newest) row. The #2958 stale-wins
  class is closed in the knowledge engine.
- **Real producer rows are keyed and survive link/unlink.**
  `knowledge-events.jsonl` rows key by `event_id` (legacy top-level `id`
  still keys); `knowledge-application.jsonl` rows use a canonical whole-row
  identity (bounded sha1, `knowledgeId` required) so distinct application
  outcomes for one entry survive while exact retries dedupe. A fresh link no
  longer silently drops source event rows and unlink copy-back no longer
  aborts the whole family migration at the pre-commit validator.

### Known edges

The string fallback remains a heuristic tokenizer (the #3491/#3088 detector
programs track the deeper rewrite); this change closes the five frozen
escape classes plus the feedback-round escapes (mkdir-then-cd, grouped cd,
drive-phantom paths, torn procsub operands) and widens fail-closed
withdrawal to ambiguous
